mainEntity.name: How much does a Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine replacement cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: A rebuilt Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine typically costs £1,300-£2,800 supply-only, depending on supplier and condition. Used engines start from £800. Supply & fit adds £450-£900 labour. Main dealer replacement can exceed £4,000.

mainEntity.name: What are the most common Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine problems?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY / EP6DTS) engine problems are timing chain stretch and tensioner failure causing cold-start rattle, high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) failure causing hard starting and misfires, carbon buildup on intake valves from direct injection, and turbocharger oil feed line leaks. The 5FY 175hp variant is particularly susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine on a Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine is worthwhile if the vehicle is otherwise sound and the replacement cost stays below the vehicle's value. With 207 GTi values typically £2,500-£7,000, a rebuilt engine at £1,300-£2,800 represents a significant investment but often makes sense for well-maintained examples. For sub-£3,000 examples, a used engine from £800 may be more economical.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine last?

acceptedAnswer.text: With proper maintenance, the Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY / EP6DTS) engine can reach 100,000-130,000 miles. However, timing chain issues can appear as early as 40,000 miles, and HPFP failure from 50,000 miles. Regular oil changes with correct PSA-approved oil, timely timing chain replacement and HPFP monitoring are essential for longevity.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP and 207 GT 1.6 THP?

acceptedAnswer.text: The 207 GTi uses the 5FY (EP6DTS) engine producing 175hp, while the 207 GT uses the EP6DT (5FX) engine producing 150hp. Both use the same 1.6L Prince architecture, but the 5FY has a higher-output calibration, larger turbocharger and more aggressive engine mapping. The GTi also features an overboost function taking torque to 260 Nm. The 5FY is also more susceptible to HPFP failure and timing chain guide wear due to higher cylinder pressures.

mainEntity.name: How do I find my Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine code?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine code is 5FY (EP6DTS / N14). It appears on the VIN plate under the bonnet, stamped on the engine block, or on your V5C registration document section D.2. Enter your reg above for instant verification.

historyTimeline.h2: Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Peugeot 207 GTi (also known as the 207 RC in some markets) was the performance flagship of the 207 range, powered by the 1.6-litre THP (Turbo High Pressure) engine - a direct-injection turbocharged four-cylinder jointly developed by PSA and BMW. Producing 175hp (128kW) and 240 Nm of torque (with an overboost function raising torque to 260 Nm), the 5FY (EP6DTS) engine delivered genuine hot-hatch performance. Launched in 2007, the 207 GTi featured a five-speed manual gearbox, 0-62mph in 7.1 seconds and a top speed of 137mph. However, its Prince engine architecture has well-documented weaknesses - particularly timing chain tensioner failure, high-pressure fuel pump problems and carbon buildup - that continue to drive replacement enquiries today.

milestones.description: **2007** - Peugeot 207 GTi launched with 1.6 THP 175 (5FY / EP6DTS) producing 175hp
**2008** - Minor ECU refinements; timing chain tensioner issues begin to surface
**2009** - Revised timing chain components introduced for later production models
**2010** - HPFP and turbo oil feed line updates for improved reliability
**2012** - 207 GTi production ends; 1.6 THP continues in 208 GTi and other PSA models

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every 5FY engine fitted to the Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP (5FY / EP6DTS) is a thrilling hot hatch when running well, but its Prince engine architecture - shared with BMW and Mini - has well-documented weaknesses. Timing chain tensioner failure, high-pressure fuel pump problems and carbon buildup are the primary drivers of replacement enquiries. The 5FY 175hp variant is particularly susceptible to timing chain issues and HPFP failure due to higher cylinder pressures. Every rebuilt Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Timing Chain Failure - Why Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP Engines Rattle and Fail
problems.rootCause: The Prince engine's timing chain tensioner can lose hydraulic pressure, allowing chain slack to develop. Over time, the chain stretches and the plastic guides wear, leading to rattling on cold start and, in severe cases, chain jump and valve-piston contact. A stretched timing chain is notoriously difficult to diagnose externally. Owner reviews confirm cam chain tensioner replacement under warranty is common.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of chain, tensioner (revised), guides and VANOS sprockets
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught early; prevents catastrophic failure; some owners report 2k repair bills for timing work

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with upgraded timing components, new HPFP and turbo seals, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Required if chain has jumped or caused valve damage

problems.recommendation: If your Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP exhibits the characteristic cold-start rattle or chain slap when cold and idling, address it immediately. A timing chain kit replacement is significantly cheaper than a full engine replacement. Once the rattle is constant or accompanied by loss of power and a "Depollution Fault" warning, the chain has likely jumped - at that stage, a rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components is the safest option.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt 5FY Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP engine prices

problems.h4: High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP Engines Fail to Start and Run Roughly
problems.rootCause: The Bosch HPFP's internal cam follower wears prematurely, causing metal contamination to circulate through the high-pressure fuel rail and injectors. Symptoms include hard starting, rough idle, misfires and, in severe cases, complete non-start. The 5FY 175hp variant is particularly susceptible due to higher fuel pressures. Fault code P0087 (low fuel pressure) is a common indicator.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace pump, flush fuel lines, replace inline filter
repairOptions.longevity: Only viable if caught before metal debris reaches injectors

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Full rebuild with upgraded HPFP and cleaned rail, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Essential when metallic particles have contaminated the combustion chambers; HPFP replacement has been known to fix misfires

problems.recommendation: HPFP failure on the Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP is catastrophic if delayed. If diagnostic codes show fuel rail pressure deviation alongside metallic fuel, budget for a full engine replacement immediately - repairing injectors alone will not prevent repeat failure. The 5FY 175hp variant is especially susceptible; HPFP failure is one of the most common reasons for 207 GTi engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Find specialist Peugeot 207 GTi 1.6 THP rebuilt engines with upgraded HPFP

problems.h4: Carbon Buildup - Why Direct Injection Causes Power Loss and Rough Idle
problems.rootCause: Direct injection petrol engines do not wash the intake valves with fuel, allowing carbon deposits from the PCV system to accumulate on valve stems and seats. This restricts airflow, causing rough idle, hesitation, reduced power and increased fuel consumption. Owners report lumpy idle that worsens as the engine warms up.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Media blasting of intake valves to remove carbon deposits
repairOptions.longevity: Effective if caught before valve damage occurs

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete rebuilt unit with refreshed valvetrain and intake system
repairOptions.longevity: Only necessary if carbon buildup has caused valve or piston damage

problems.recommendation: Carbon buildup is a known characteristic of direct injection engines. A professional walnut blast cleaning every 40,000-60,000 miles is a worthwhile preventative measure. If the engine has been running poorly for an extended period, carbon scoring may have damaged cylinder walls - in which case a rebuilt unit is the only reliable fix.
